In withPreview (scripts/browser.mjs:29-35, and the same code in the bootstrap template at lines 30-32), the readiness loop runs at most 100 times. Each pass polls fetch(url) and sleeps 100ms. The loop throws &#39;preview startup failed&#39; if the child exits, and &#39;preview readiness failed&#39; when the attempts run out. (2) Both verify.mjs (line 5) and inspect-presentation.mjs (line 11) `await command(&#39;npm&#39;,[&#39;run&#39;,&#39;build&#39;])` before calling withPreview. command() resolves only when the build process exits with code 0, so the preview never starts during the build. The bootstrap template copies match on those same lines. (3) Readiness polls HTTP and never parses the server&#39;s printed output, so the ANSI and chunk-splitting clause does not apply. judges{"demo-integration":[{"id":"demo-scene-kit-api-use","verdict":"pass","basis":"consensus-pass","votes":[{"id":"demo-scene-kit-api-use","verdict":"pass","rationale":"Talk.tsx hands the step list and title to the kit&#39;s Presentation. Box is the only component that applies the motion `layout` prop, and Arrow, Frame, Label and SymbolChip all delegate to it.","evidence":["Talk.tsx renders `&lt;Presentation className=&quot;making&quot; steps={STEPS} title=... initialMode=&quot;browse&quot; /&gt;` imported from &#39;../../presentation-kit&#39;.","Scene.tsx imports Box, Arrow, Frame, Label, SceneLayer, SymbolChip, ENTER_DELAY and ENTER_T from the kit. EvolvingScene is typed with SceneProps&lt;Payload&gt; and wraps its output in SceneLayer.","steps/index.ts builds `Step&lt;Payload&gt;[]` objects with Scene: EvolvingScene, groupKey and payload, using the kit&#39;s Step type.","Box.tsx renders `motion.div` with `layout` and the shared LAYOUT_T/EASE transition. Arrow, Frame, Label and SymbolChip are thin wrappers around Box.","Presentation.tsx wires usePresentationNav, Stage, Header, Footer and Toc."],"citations":["src/presentations/how-to-make-a-presentation/Talk.tsx","src/presentations/how-to-make-a-presentation/steps/Scene.tsx","src/presentations/how-to-make-a-presentation/steps/index.ts","src/presentation-kit/Presentation.tsx","src/presentation-kit/Stage.tsx","src/presentation-kit/nodes/Box.tsx","src/presentation-kit/nodes/Arrow.tsx","src/presentation-kit/nodes/Frame.tsx","src/presentation-kit/nodes/Label.tsx","src/presentation-kit/nodes/SymbolChip.tsx","src/presentation-kit/nodes/SceneLayer.tsx"],"family":"claude","model":"claude-sonnet-5-5","effort":"high","panel_index":0},{"id":"demo-scene-kit-api-use","verdict":"pass","rationale":"Talk hands its steps, title, initialMode and className to the kit&#39;s Presentation instead of reimplementing orchestration. The shared Scene builds its output from the kit&#39;s SceneLayer, Box, Arrow, Frame, Label and SymbolChip, and takes ENTER_DELAY and ENTER_T from the kit. The review guidance says a warning identifies an element by the step plus, for each element, its visible text. The other options (accessible name, stable hook or data attribute, selector path) apply only to an element without visible text. In scripts/diagnostics.mjs, control participants get only identity(el) as their id: data-entity, else the element id, else the first data-presentation-* attribute name, else the tag name. What fails is the clause that the warning must identify the overlapping elements. The guidance says an element with visible text is identified by its visible text. Only an element without visible text may be named by an accessible name, hook, or selector. Control participants are built at diagnostics.mjs:38 with identity(el) alone. identity (line 28) returns data-entity, else the id, else the first data-presentation-* attribute name, else the tag name, and never adds visible text. Only text-node participants (line 35) carry text. The candidate renders text-bearing chrome with no data-entity or id. The progress buttons show the numbers 1-9 (Footer.tsx:5) and the TOC entries show era names (Toc.tsx:5). An overlap with one of these controls&#39; boxes would therefore print the bare hook `data-presentation-progress` or `data-presentation-toc-entry`, which is the same for all nine dots or all the entries. The focused test confirms this. The padded button displays &#39;Next&#39;, yet the test expects `overlap padding-label.*padded-control` and asserts the output does NOT match `padded-control:Next` (inspection.test.mjs:15-16, 32). So the bounds warning never names the control&#39;s visible text. Judge B&#39;s reason is borne out by this material, and it decides the identification clause. Judges A and C read the warning as naming the elements: A said ids come from data-entity, id, or a hook, and C said &#39;Ids combine data-entity, id or hook with the visible text&#39;. C&#39;s claim holds only for text-range participants (line 35), not control participants (line 38). A&#39;s reading lets a hook stand in for a text-bearing element, which the guidance allows only for textless elements. (1) Readiness is bounded. In withPreview (scripts/browser.mjs:29-35, and the same code in the bootstrap template at lines 30-32), the readiness loop runs at most 100 times. Each pass polls fetch(url) and sleeps 100ms. The loop throws &#39;preview startup failed&#39; if the child exits, and &#39;preview readiness failed&#39; when the attempts run out. (2) Both verify.mjs (line 5) and inspect-presentation.mjs (line 11) `await command(&#39;npm&#39;,[&#39;run&#39;,&#39;build&#39;])` before calling withPreview. command() resolves only when the build process exits with code 0, so the preview never starts during the build. The bootstrap template copies match on those same lines. (3) Readiness polls HTTP and never parses the server&#39;s printed output, so the ANSI and chunk-splitting clause does not apply. Every browser test starts its process tree through harness run(&#39;npm&#39;,[&#39;run&#39;,&#39;verify&#39;|&#39;inspect&#39;],...). package.json:14-15 shows that npm only wraps `node scripts/verify.mjs`, and that script spawns the Vite preview as its own separate child (browser.mjs:24). Nothing in the started tree turns that signal into cleanup of the preview. verify.mjs (quoted in full, lines 1-65) and browser.mjs (quoted in full, lines 1-88) install no process.on(&#39;SIGTERM&#39;/&#39;SIGINT&#39;) handler. The withPreview `finally` (browser.mjs:41-58), the only code that kills the Vite child, runs only when the async flow unwinds. It does not run when the Node process is terminated by a signal. The preview child is spawned without detached or a process group (browser.mjs:24), and nothing kills a group. So when a test times out, only the npm wrapper is killed and the vite preview server keeps running. That is the scenario the guidance names: &#39;a test kills only the npx wrapper and leaves the preview server running&#39;. assertStopped (harness.mjs:22-27) checks cleanup only after a normal exit and never runs on the timeout rejection path. Judge A and Judge B said pass, citing freePort() and assertStopped. Their reasons are accurate but do not decide the requirement, because they cover dynamic ports and normal exits only. Neither addresses the run() timeout path, which kills just the wrapper and leaves the preview server unterminated. The review guidance says a warning identifies an element by the step plus, for each element, its visible text. The other options (accessible name, stable hook or data attribute, selector path) apply only to an element without visible text. In scripts/diagnostics.mjs, control participants get only identity(el) as their id: data-entity, else the element id, else the first data-presentation-* attribute name, else the tag name. They never get the element&#39;s visible text. Text-node participants are the only ones that carry the text, as identity:text. diagnose prints these ids as-is in &#39;overlap a.id / b.id&#39;. So when a text-bearing control&#39;s bounds collide with something, the warning leaves out the control&#39;s visible text. The INT-002 test shows exactly this. The padded button displays &#39;Next&#39;, and the test asserts the warning matches &#39;overlap padding-label.*padded-control&#39; while also asserting it does NOT match &#39;padded-control:Next&#39;. The warning therefore names the button only by its id, with no visible text.
